message:
docs(history): five suites are invisible in the total, which is why it never moved

Chasing a 1820 vs 1823 difference, I recorded per-suite counts for the first
time. Five suites print no ^PASS lines at all -- gdi_capture_process,
host_bgra_scale, host_encode_epoch, viewer_udp_recovery, capture_cadence_gate --
so they contribute zero whether they pass or fail.

Which means "64 suites, 1820, no failures" was two instruments in one sentence:
the failure count comes from exit codes and has nothing to do with 1820. Put side
by side they read as one piece of evidence.

It also answers something I never asked in #497. Four suites went red and the
total did not move, and I wrote down that they were red without wondering why the
number was unaffected. This is why.

The +3 is still unexplained; update_manifest_test was 85 on both sides. The
per-suite numbers now exist to decompose it against, and until then the total is
not evidence. The verdict on this work rests on execution-level assertions -- the
old routing reproduced, real bytes replaced, access-denied asserted in both
directions -- not on a sum.

Also recorded: the verifier's run failed gdi_capture_process at 40.65 fps where
mine passed, with the live host capturing the same screen at the time. Separated
as environmental and left unverified rather than called unrelated -- confirming it
would mean stopping the live app, which is not allowed.
